text: Let's name the real currency Fabric compute actually runs on — capacities and SKUs.

Recall Lesson 1's preview — a capacity is a managed compute pool. That pool is measured in capacity units, one number, spent by whichever engine is actually working. Every engine shares the same pool — there's no separate budget per item type.
An F-SKU is simply a fixed number of capacity units, purchased as one unit — Fabric's real answer to Databricks Lesson 4's VM-size decision, just chosen once per capacity instead of once per cluster.

And bursting lets a job briefly use more than the capacity nominally provides, while smoothing spreads the real cost out over time. Together, an occasional heavy job doesn't force you to permanently buy a bigger SKU.
One shared pool, sized to sustained load, not worst-case peaks. Next lesson: Git integration and deployment pipelines, real version control for Fabric items.
